name: Sparse Representation Analysis
description: Uses sparse coding and dictionary learning to detect representation anomalies in AI images (Wright et al., 2009).
mechanism:
This method applies sparse representation theory following Wright et al. (2009) and Elad & Aharon (2006) for forensic analysis:

1. **Dictionary Learning**: A redundant dictionary D ∈ ℝⁿˣᴷ (K >> n, overcomplete) is learned from natural image patches via K-SVD algorithm. Each atom captures a characteristic local structure (edge, texture, smooth region) found in authentic images.

2. **Sparse Coding**: For each image patch y, the sparsest representation α is found via: min‖α‖₀ s.t. ‖y − Dα‖₂ ≤ ε. In practice, OMP (Orthogonal Matching Pursuit) or LASSO provides an approximate solution. Natural image patches admit highly sparse representations (few active atoms).

3. **Representation Residual Analysis**: The residual r = ‖y − Dα‖₂ measures how well each patch fits the natural image dictionary. Authentic image patches yield low residuals, while AI-generated patches — containing artifacts outside the natural image manifold — produce elevated residuals.

4. **Sparsity Map Construction**: A spatial map of sparsity levels (‖α‖₀) and residuals across the image reveals regions inconsistent with natural image statistics. Manipulated or AI-generated regions typically require more dictionary atoms (lower sparsity) yet still produce higher residuals.

5. **Anomaly Scoring**: The joint distribution of sparsity and residuals across all patches is compared to the expected distribution for natural images. Systematic deviations — particularly elevated residuals in textured regions that should be well-represented by the learned dictionary — indicate synthetic generation.
parameters: Analysis type: automated statistical\nScore range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)\nMinimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations: • Accuracy varies with input quality\n• Best used in combination with other methods\n• May require calibration for new AI models

references.title: Wright, J. et al. (2009). Robust Face Recognition via Sparse Representation. IEEE TPAMI.
Elad, M. & Aharon, M. (2006). Image Denoising via Sparse and Redundant Representations. IEEE TIP.
